Data Appreciation · Week 3 · Title

Saving, storage and backups

Know where your work is saved — on the device, a flash drive or the cloud — and keep a backup before you need it.

Next Generation Genius · Year 1 · Foundation

Data Appreciation · Week 3 · Goals

By the end of today

  • Tell device storage, removable storage and cloud storage apart
  • Use Save and Save As correctly
  • Make a backup plan with the 3-2-1 rule
Data Appreciation · Week 3 · Idea 1

Understand it

Where can a file live?

  • On the device — the phone or laptop itself. Fast, but lost with the device.
  • Removable storage — a flash drive (USB) or memory card. Carry it anywhere; easy to lose.
  • The cloud — your files kept on a company's computers over the internet (Google Drive, OneDrive, iCloud). Reached from any device, but needs data and a strong password.

Save keeps changes in the same file. Save As makes a new copy with a new name or place — use it before big changes, so the old version survives.

Data Appreciation · Week 3 · Idea 2

Understand it

The 3-2-1 rule: keep 3 copies of anything important, on 2 different kinds of storage, with 1 somewhere else (the cloud, or away from home). Phones are lost, stolen and dropped; a project that exists in one place is a project you can lose the day before it is due.

The 3-2-1 backup rule

Data Appreciation · Week 3 · Key words

Key words

Cloud storage
files kept on servers you reach over the internet
Save As
save a copy with a new name or place
Backup
an extra copy kept in case the original is lost
Sync
keeping the same files up to date on several devices
Data Appreciation · Week 3 · Practice

Now you do it

  1. Save a file twice: once with Save, once with Save As to a new name
  2. Copy it to a flash drive or cloud drive
  3. Write your own 3-2-1 backup plan

Data Appreciation · Week 3 · Assessment

How you will be assessed

  • Your only copy of a project is on your phone. Which change makes it safest?
  • Follow the NCSC backup steps on one of your devices (with a parent if it is theirs). Paste a screenshot of the backup turned on, and say what it backs up.
  • Write your own 3-2-1 backup plan: the three copies, the two kinds of storage, and the one kept elsewhere.

Your work is marked against the rubric, and you may be asked to explain your choices. Show your own thinking.
